source_texts: You are reviewing a small software service. Explain how to make it reliable. The service receives customer requests, reads a local database, and writes a report. A useful design records completed work, retries temporary failures, and gives each request a clear identity. Separate the time spent waiting for storage from the time spent computing results. When comparing two implementations, hold the input and output requirements fixed.

You are helping a student plan a community library. Describe practical choices for the project. The library has a fixed budget, limited shelves, and volunteers working different hours. Books need labels, a borrowing record, and a clear process for returns. Measure whether readers can find a book quickly and whether volunteers can keep records accurate. Start with a small usable collection and expand after the first month of feedback.

You are explaining a city transport plan. Discuss how to compare two bus routes. The city has narrow roads, busy schools, and passengers who travel at different times. A fair comparison uses the same number of vehicles and records passenger waiting time. Check the morning and evening periods separately, because averages can hide delays. Describe the cost of the change and the improvement that residents would experience.
